name: shimmer-loader
title: Shimmer Loader
description: A stack of monospace progress bars that a purple shimmer sweeps across while the labels cycle and the percentages and token counts climb, then restart from zero when finished.
use: An AI or devtool screen wants a distinctive charging-up indicator with labels and token figures instead of a plain bar.
avoid: It loops on its own and reports fake progress, so it must not stand in for a real measured task or a cancel control.
a11y: There is no progressbar role or live value, so screen readers get the label text but not the percentage, and the loop ignores reduced motion. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: On a black panel, three stacked strips of purple gradient cells each hold a centred monospace label and percentage. A bright violet shimmer band moves across each strip, a small purple glyph sits at the left and a dim '0.1k' style token count at the right.
behaves: Each bar counts up from zero to 100% over a few seconds while the shimmer sweeps and the label word changes in stages. When a bar completes it restarts from zero, so the three strips loop continuously.
customise: Labels, icon glyphs, duration, token target, whether percent shows, font size, cell padding and text colour are props; the purple gradient maths is fixed in the source.
weight: moderate: A requestAnimationFrame loop recolours every cell of three strips forty times a second.
demo: Three loaders labelled Analysing, Booting or Initializing, and Syncing or Onboarding, with token targets.
issues: The token counter at the right is a very dim purple and is barely readable.
polishWhy: A distinctive terminal look with a smooth shimmer; the token counter is too faint to read.
